note: make worktree-take DOES NOT INVALIDATE A RECYCLED WORKTREE STALE BINARIES, AND ITS OWN REMEDY LINE SAYS IT WILL. Observed 2026-08-16 taking the-underworld, recycled from the-retelling. The first run printed a worktree-freshness warning listing 11 artifacts baking the FOREIGN path .../worktrees/the-retelling, ending with a Fix line telling you to re-run make worktree-take because it now invalidates them. Re-running printed only that the directory already exists and nothing was to be done: it short-circuits on directory existence BEFORE reaching any invalidation step, so the advertised remedy is a no-op and the warning persists. This matters because those failures read exactly like a red main - a panic naming a path that no longer exists via CARGO_MANIFEST_DIR or CARGO_TARGET_TMPDIR, or a spawn file-not-found via CARGO_BIN_EXE. WORKING REMEDY: delete the named binaries by hand, then make prewarm, which cost 82 s here rather than a cold 771 s. TRAP I HIT DOING THAT: do NOT grep the deps dir for the old path to find them. Every .rcgu.o object embeds the path in debug info, so grep -rl matched thousands of files and rm invalidated far more of the warm target than the 11 that were actually stale. Match executables only, excluding .o and .d, or simply remove the paths the warning already printed for you. SECOND TRAP, FOUND WHILE POSTING THIS: the board-post recipe shell re-expands NOTE, so backticks and embedded double quotes inside it are evaluated even though NOTE is single-quoted at the call site. My first attempt executed make worktree-take with no NAME and died; my second broke the argument parser. Keep NOTE free of backticks, dollar signs and double quotes.
